facts.text: Glazier was platted in 1887 on Johnson’s ranchland as the railroad reached the town, turning it into a key shipping point for cattle and wheat.
A violent tornado on April 9, 1947 destroyed every building in Glazier except one house and the jail, claiming twelve lives and leaving only a post office and three businesses.
By 1959 the post office closed, and by 1984 Glazier reported only twenty residents and no businesses, marking a sharp decline after the tornado.
Glazier’s location north of the Canadian River made it an ideal shipping point for cattlemen, especially when the river rose during the rainy season.
The extension of the Santa Fe line in 1916 from Shattuck, Oklahoma, to Spearman, Texas, drew away much of the cattle and wheat trade that Glazier had depended on.
